radiology_report:
Department of Radiology
UMCG (Groningen)
Date: 28 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 5.7 ng/mL, suspected prostate cancer

FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 42.59 mL in volume. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a well-defined, hypointense lesion in the peripheral zone of the mid right prostate, measuring approximately 12 mm in maximal diameter. This lesion shows restricted diffusion on DWI with corresponding high signal on the ADC map and early, intense enhancement on DCE sequences. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is visualized. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous metastases are identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the peripheral zone, mid right prostate.
PSA density: 0.134 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cTx.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8136245.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a rising PSA trend, measured at 4.6 ng/mL in December 2023, up from 1.4 ng/mL in October 2022. A multiparametric MRI was arranged, showing a PI-RADS 5 lesion. The patient underwent a targeted biopsy which confirmed prostate cancer. Referred to urology for further management discussion.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (28 Oct 2024): The histological examination reveals adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. The growth pattern is acinar. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, mid right.

Summary: The biopsy findings have remained stable across the single timepoint, showing ISUP grade group 2 disease without high-risk features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
